title: A Group Breathwork Intervention to Improve Chronic Cancer-Related Pain in Solid Tumor Cancer Survivors
official: Group Breathwork for Chronic Cancer-Related Pain
summary: This clinical trial studies whether a group breathwork intervention works to improve chronic cancer-related pain (CCRP) in solid tumor cancer survivors. Advances in cancer care have allowed patients to live longer after a cancer diagnosis. However, many of those in extended survivorship continue to suffer from symptoms associated with cancer or its treatment, including CCRP. Chronic pain is highly disabling and interferes with the ability of an individual to engage in daily activities and enjoy a normal life. During the group breathwork intervention session in this trial, attendees are guided through breathwork in which they breathe in a continuous rhythm without pausing between inhale and exhale. This breathing may cause different physical sensations or emotions which may help to relax the body and release tension. A group breathwork intervention may improve CCRP in solid tumor cancer survivors.
criteria:
Inclusion Criteria:

* Men and women 18-70 years of age
* History of any solid tumor cancer type
* Extended survivorship (i.e., within the 5-year period following the cessation of initial active cancer treatment)
* Self-reported chronic pain that has persisted for at least the past 3 months and that the participant attributes to their cancer and/or cancer treatment
* Average pain intensity of \>= 4/10 for the past month due to CCRP

Exclusion Criteria:

* Neurological disease (e.g. Parkinson's, multiple sclerosis, epilepsy, history of seizures) or moderate or severe symptoms from a previous brain injury, including stroke and traumatic brain injury
* Respiratory disorder (e.g., chronic obstructive pulmonary disease) or moderate to severe asthma within the past 12 months
* Activity limiting heart disease including cardiovascular or peripheral arterial disease
* Uncontrolled hypertension (i.e. systolic blood pressure \[SBP\]/diastolic blood pressure \[DBP\] of \> 160/95) or orthostatic hypotension (e.g., issues with fainting)
* Serious psychiatric disorder (e.g., schizophrenia, panic disorder) or mental health issues (e.g., post-traumatic stress disorder \[PTSD\]) requiring hospitalization within the past 12 months or currently on antipsychotic medications
* Cognitive impairment or factors that would preclude comprehension of material and/or full participation in the study
* Glaucoma or detached retina
* Pregnant
* Any significant comorbidities or other reasons that, in the opinion of the investigators, could interfere with the study or lead to deleterious effects for the participant
